requirements.title: Command Code executable name is cmd, which collides with the Windows command interpreter
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:51 executableName - case .commandcode returns "cmd"

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:239-247 fallbackExecutables for commandcode - the comment names "cmd" as the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" as the package's own names
requirements.action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH under the bare name cmd, then walks the commandcode fallback list.
requirements.expected_result: The bare name searched first is exactly "cmd". The same string is the Binary path placeholder for the Command Code section.
side_effects: A PATH walk plus the fallback candidate walk.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY AND COLLISION. On Windows the bare name cmd resolves to the system command interpreter cmd.exe on the machine PATH, so a direct PATHEXT lookup finds the wrong program and would make Command Code read as installed on every Windows PC. The source contains no identity check, so the rule for distinguishing them is an open decision and must not be guessed. Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%System32cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%SysWOW64cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture plus an interaction test proving a system cmd.exe is never accepted as Command Code
requirements.open_question: How a Windows build distinguishes the Command Code CLI from the system command interpreter, given that the bare name "cmd" resolves to cmd.exe on every Windows PATH and the source contains no identity check. Not resolvable from source; needs an owner decision on the probe (for example a --version identity check, or dropping the bare name on Windows).

requirements.preconditions: A Keychain write of an API key has just returned.
requirements.action: storeAPIKeyFallback runs for that provider.
requirements.expected_result: Each of the four API key inputs runs the same three lines on change, guarded so the initial Keychain read does not trigger it and so an unchanged value does nothing. setAPIKey trims the value of whitespace and newlines and returns whether the Keychain KEPT it; note an empty key deletes the item and returns TRUE, so clearing a key also clears the mirror. When the return is FALSE, and only then, storeAPIKeyFallback writes the key to the matching UserDefaults key - deepseekAPIKey, metaAPIKey, zaiAPIKey or commandcodeAPIKey. When it is true the EMPTY STRING is written to that same key, which removes any mirror an earlier refusal left behind. The mirror is written UNTRIMMED, from the input property, while the Keychain stores the trimmed value, so the two stores can hold different strings for the same key. On read, APIKeychain.key(for:fallback:) prefers a non-empty Keychain value and returns the mirror otherwise, making the two a single logical slot.
side_effects: SECURITY-RELEVANT: a provider API key is written to disk in plain text, in the app's user defaults, readable by any process running as the user.
requirements.persistence: UserDefaults keys deepseekAPIKey, metaAPIKey, zaiAPIKey, commandcodeAPIKey.
failure_cases: Nothing tells the user their key is now stored in the clear.
A key with leading or trailing whitespace is mirrored with that whitespace while the Keychain copy is trimmed.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY AND POLICY DECISION. This is the one half of the API key store that must NOT be transliterated. The port's own rules require SecretStore (DPAPI through Electron safeStorage) and say that when protected storage is unavailable the app must fail and say so, never fall back to plain text. Reproducing the mirror faithfully would write user API keys to disk unencrypted on every Windows PC where DPAPI is unavailable. The clearing half of the rule - writing the empty string on success - is safe and should be kept whatever is decided about the mirror itself.
requirements.verification_method: unit test with a refusing secret store, asserting both the mirror write and the clear-on-success
